query: Single-phase ZrB2 benefits from strong Zr–B and B–B interactions and a high melting point, but it requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and does not readily meet application requirements on its own. Earlier studies sought to lower the required temperature, yet the resulting materials remained vulnerable to high-temperature oxidation or liquid plating-metal corrosion, while reported preparation temperatures generally remained above 1700 °C. Under the constraints of lower-temperature manufacture, adequate strength and structural integrity, oxidation durability, and prolonged service in a liquid plating bath, what single intervention could overcome these limitations? Provide one hypothesis specifying the intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome compared with single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens, applicable preparation and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment evaluating final body quality, structural integrity, oxidation, and liquid-metal corrosion that would falsify the hypothesis if its predictions were not observed.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating 5 vol% nanoscale SiC into ZrB₂ and densifying by spark-plasma sintering at 1600 °C will yield a >97 % dense composite that exhibits higher strength, lower high-temperature oxidation, and reduced liquid Al infiltration compared with single-phase ZrB₂ sintered at 2300 °C or lower-temperature ZrB₂ specimens.
generation.material_initial_state: Commercial ZrB₂ powder (∼2 µm) with no sintering additives
generation.intervention: Add 5 vol% nanoscale SiC and perform spark-plasma sintering under vacuum (<10 Pa) at 1600 °C for 10 min with 50 MPa uniaxial pressure
generation.conditions: Heating rate 100 °C/min to 1600 °C, hold 10 min, vacuum <10 Pa, 50 MPa pressure
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform dispersion of SiC nanoparticles at ZrB₂ grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: During SPS, transient Si-rich liquid phases promote rapid densification and SiC particles pin grains; upon high-temperature exposure in air, residual SiC oxidizes to a continuous SiO₂-rich scale that impedes O₂ ingress, and the robust oxide/nitride network at grain boundaries resists molten Al penetration
generation.predicted_outcome: Density >97 % theoretical; room-temperature flexural strength >350 MPa; mass gain <50 mg/cm² after 50 h at 1200 °C in air; molten Al infiltration depth <10 µm after 100 h at 750 °C
generation.baseline: Single-phase ZrB₂ sintered at 2300 °C: >98 % density, ∼300 MPa flexural strength, mass gain >200 mg/cm² at 1200 °C, Al infiltration >100 µm
generation.boundary: Applicable for SPS temperatures ≤1700 °C and service conditions up to 1200 °C in air and up to 800 °C in molten Al baths
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; long-term thermal cycling stability of the SiC/SiO₂ network and behavior in Al-Si alloys remain to be validated

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three discs: (1) ZrB₂+5 vol% SiC by SPS at 1600 °C; (2) single-phase ZrB₂ by conventional sintering at 2300 °C; (3) single-phase ZrB₂ by SPS at 1700 °C. Measure density, flexural strength, oxidation mass gain (1200 °C, air, 50 h), and molten Al infiltration depth (750 °C, 100 h).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SiC-doped specimen achieves density <97 %, flexural strength <350 MPa, oxidation mass gain >50 mg/cm², or Al infiltration >10 µm, the hypothesis is falsified.
